newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traffic accidents, deaths plunge in France.
newsitem.headline: Traffic accidents, deaths plunge in France.

text.p: The number of traffic accidents in France fell last year to the lowest level in 25 years but the country remains a more dangerous place to drive than some other European states, the government said on Wednesday.
"This is a very good result, although France remains well above some of our European neighbours," Transport Minister Bernard Pons told reporters.
The government said there were 125,406 traffic accidents last year, a six percent drop from 1995.
The number of deaths fell by four percent to 8,080 while the number of injuries declined by six percent to 170,117, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said .
Lamassoure said the biggest improvement was among young people aged 15-24 and gave credit to more of them wearing protective helmets while riding motorcycles and taking other safety precautions.
The accident toll declined for all categories including bicycles, pedestrians, motorcyclists and lorry drivers as well as cars.
